title: The Field Is Ours
clue: A gate that only opens for the two of you, and a landscape with no one else in it.
reveal: Rent a secure private field for half an hour and give your dog a quiet estate with no other dogs, no strangers and no instructions. You check the fence, then you simply follow.
objective: Visit a booked, secure private field, check the boundary together, then spend ten silent minutes following your dog's lead.
instructions: Find a private dog field you can book by the half hour (many areas have rentable fenced fields), or ask a landowner you know for a secure paddock. Confirm it is yours alone for the slot, and note the fence height, gates and rules.
Pack a harness, leash, water and bowl, waste bags, a towel and a favorite toy. If your dog's recall is not rock solid, bring a lightweight long line.
Arrive on time. Keep your dog on leash from the car to the gate, and close the gate behind you before anything comes off.
Do a fence lap on leash first, checking for gaps, holes, broken wire, glass, burrows and wet or boggy ground. If anything looks unsafe, tell the host and call it off.
Open the field to your dog: unclip only if it is fully enclosed and your dog is reliable, or use the long line. Let them choose where to go first.
The Silent Visit: for ten minutes, stop giving instructions. No ball, no phone, no commands. Stay in the open, follow at a distance and keep your eyes on your dog.
Whatever your dog does next, from a sniff to a sprint to a lie-down, is the main event. Join in only if they invite it. Stop when they do.
Clip the leash back on before the gate, offer water, towel off muddy paws and buckle up for the trip home.
twist: The Silent Visit: after a quick fence check you give no instructions for ten minutes, and the field, the route and the pace all belong to your dog.
variations: Easier: a quiet fenced area you know is empty, such as a closed school field with permission, on leash or long line.
Seated version: take a camp chair, sit at the gate and let your dog roam the field while you watch.
Shorter version: a fifteen-minute slot with just the fence lap and a few minutes of the Silent Visit.
Companion version: a trusted friend sits with you; there are no other dogs and no unplanned introductions.
completion: You have checked the field together and spent your Silent Visit following your dog, ending when they were ready.
photoIdea: Your dog far across the open field, small against the grass, taken from where you were standing.
memoryPrompt: What did your dog head for first when the whole field was theirs?
substitutes: A large bottle and a collapsible cup for water

reservation.note: Book a secure private field slot ahead and confirm it is exclusive to you, with fencing, gate and pet rules checked.

safety: Walk the fence first; leave if there are gaps, wire, glass, deep mud, ponds or livestock.
Use a long line unless the field is fully enclosed and your dog reliably returns; no retractable leashes.
Bring water and shade; skip hot days. Restrain your dog in the car and never leave them in it.
